Inglewood, California
  February 11, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, February 11, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:03 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency officials and personnel present for closed session were as
follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:03 p.m. for Closed Session
Item No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, Finance Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at
the hour of 2:03 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority
Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman/Finance  Authority
  Chairman/Parking  Authority  Chairman/Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority  Members/Finance  Authority
  Members/Parking  Authority  Members/Joint
  Powers Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority / Finance Authority / Parking
Authority /Joint Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  1
 February 11, 2020

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking
  Authority Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there
  were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  No name given, Representative for Congresswoman Maxine Waters, stated that
  she is here to observe the City Council meeting, and to listen to Wanda Brown’s
  comments.

  Maria (No last name given), South Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB)
  representative, gave a brief overview on the SBWIB quarterly report which
  summarizes the meeting activities, and program accomplishments of January 16,
  2020

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Dotson that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated February 6, 2020, in the amount of
  $4,338,309.61 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Dotson that the Minutes for the Council Meeting held on
  January 28, 2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.
101  RESOLUTION NOT ADOPTED – RATIFYING THE APPOINTMENTS
  TO THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB).
  Staff report dated February 11, 2020, was presented recommending adoption of a
  resolution ratifying the following appointments to the South Bay Workforce
  Investment Board (SBWIB):
  1. The City of Torrance appointed Mr. Sanjay Murty, Vice President of Murti
  LLC, to serve a term of office that will end on June 30, 2023; and
  2. The City of Hawthorne appointed Ms. Hilda Shofani, Owner of Le Pain Du
  Jour, to serve a term of office that will end on June 30, 2021.

  The Resolution was not adopted.
 178  PAYMENT OF INVOICES APPROVED – DR. TERRENCE MCGEE. Staff
  report dated February 11, 2020, was presented recommending approval to pay
  invoices submitted by Dr. Terrence McGee for medical review services provided
  to the Inglewood Police Department.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve payment in the amount of
  $262. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  2
   February 11, 2020

178  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AGREEMENT NO. 20-128
  APPROVED – CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE;
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-39 ADOPTED; DIRECT FUNDS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2020-2021 AND 2021-2022 BE BUDGETED FOR GRANT-
  RELATED EXPENESES. Staff report dated February 11, 2020, was presented
  recommending approval of a Memorandum of Understanding with the State of
  California Department of Justice for acceptance of Fiscal Year 2019-2020 State
  Tobacco Grant Funds in the amount of $176,727.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Memorandum of
  Understanding Agreement No. 20-128 with the California Department of Justice;
  2) Adopt Resolution No. 20-39 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AUTHORIZING ACCEPTANCE OF
  TOBACCO GRANT FUNDS FROM THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA
  AND AMENDING THE 2019-20202

  and; 3) Direct that funds for Fiscal Years 2020-2021 and 2021-2022 be budgeted
  for grant-related expenses as part of the annual budget process. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  178  AGREEMENT NO. 20-129 APPROVED – CITY OF LOS ANGELES;
  ACCEPTANCE OF FISCAL YEAR 2019 URBAN AREA SECURITY
  INITIATIVE (UASI) GRANT APPROVED. Staff report dated February 11,
  2020, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with the City of
  Los Angeles for acceptance of Fiscal Year 2019 Urban Area Security Initiative
  (UASI) grant funds in the amount of $22,500.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 20-129 in
  the amount of $22,500; and 2) Direct that funds be budgeted for use during Fiscal
  Year 2020-2021. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

178&183  AGREEMENT NO. 19-223 APPROVED – WEST COAST LIGHTS AND
  SIRENS. Staff report dated February 11, 2020, was presented recommending
  approval to issue a purchase order to West Coast Lights and Sirens to purchase
  equipment, supplies, and services to outfit police vehicles for Fiscal Year 2019-
  2020 pursuant to the terms and conditions stated in Agreement No. 19-223.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-223 in the
  amount of $100,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.
  183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-110 APPROVED –
  KIMLEY-HORN, INC. Staff report dated February 11, 2020, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 19-110 with
  Kimley-Horn, Inc., to extend the contract by an additional year and increase the
  contract amount by $300,000 (total contract amount of $1,657,989) for design and
  engineering services for the Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Gap Closure
  Project.

  3
 February 11, 2020

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to
  Agreement No. 19-110. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 301  PUBLIC HEARING SET – CONSIDER A MODIFIED RESOLUTION TO
  REPLACE RESOLUTION NO. 19-08 FOR SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO.
  2018-007. Staff report dated February 11, 2020, was presented requesting that a
  public hearing be set to consider a modified Resolution to replace Resolution No.
  19-08 for Special Use Permit No. 2018-007, which allowed a 12-bed community
  care residential health facility at 814 North Market Street.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for February 25, 2020, at the hour of
  2:00p.m.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFIDENTIAL – CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL
  COUNSEL; NAME OF CASE: MERKURIA V. CITY OF INGLEWOOD;
  LASC CASE NO.: BC643398. Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client
  Privileged; Conference with Legal Counsel regarding Pending Litigation Pursuant
  to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Name of Case: Mekuria v. City of
  Inglewood; LASC Case No.:BC643398.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve a request for settlement. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 219  CITY TREASURER REPORTS. Wanda Brown, City Treasurer, thanked
  Congresswoman Maxine Waters for sending her representative to the City
  Council meeting. Dr. Brown read questions and provided answers to residents
  with regards to the Stadium and the 1st time Home Buyer Program.
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Robert Pullen Miles, representative for Assemblywoman Autumn Burke, invited
  the City Council and residents of Inglewood, to a “Coffee with your State
  Legislature” event to be held at the 711 located at 931 S. Prairie Avenue,
  Inglewood, CA on February 29, 2020, starting at 8:00 a.m. He commented this
  would be a great opportunity to come out and talk to your State Representative.

  Michelle Chambers, representative of the Los Angeles County Tax Assessors
  Office informed the City Council that February 15, 2020, is the deadline for
  Inglewood homeowners to apply for the home owner’s tax exemption for Los
  Angeles County.

  Ray Davis thanked the City Council for their prayers and well wishes during his
  recent illness and hospitalization. He commented he is eternally grateful for the
  City of Inglewood.

  (No name given) spoke regarding the hit and run of Loretta Andrews at the corner
  of 84th and Van Ness. She stated that Loretta, a mother of five, did not deserve
  this senseless act. She asked the City Council to accept responsibility for this
  tragedy.

  Willie Agee commented that the hit and run that occurred was tragic, and he does
  not believe the City should accept responsibility.

  4
 February 11, 2020

  Aunt of Loretta Andrews, who was struck and killed at the intersection of 84th and
  Van Ness, asked the City Council to please help the family in seeking justice for
  this crime.

  (No name given) commented she is seeking justice for Loretta Andrew. She
  stated that she is reaching out to the City Council to help bring the persons
  responsible for this crime to justice.

  Stuart Bailey thanked Council Member Dotson for the shredding event in District
  1. He stated that this is a service that everyone needs and can appreciate.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned in memory of Lorretta Andrews, Bob Bacharch, and Johnny
  Lathern at the hour of 2:46 p.m.

  Approved this 25th day of February, 2020.

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
